g.text: (d) What the floor replaced, and what it costs us

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: F1. The envelope of panel (a) is FIVE identical retrains of ONE configuration at ONE seed on ONE stack (D1 `programme_only`, seed 42, GPU non-determinism the only source of

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: variation), read out by v2/research/rebase/d1_envelope_readout.py, which imports every statistic from calibra. It is a FLOOR twice over: programme_only is this project's stable

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: arm, and same-seed repeats exclude seed variation entirely. It cannot separate rank-specific variance from stack non-determinism, architecture or schedule. Statistic R1 (Roy &

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: Vetterli order-1, centred), block confound-residualised for every D2 and D1-B point and RAW for the Phase 1b point, which is judged against the RAW-block floor of 3.111x rather

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: than the residualised 3.295x - and the Phase 1b arms were never verified matched (draft 3.4). Panel (b)'s x-axis is a ratio of two R1 values within one comparison; no two rank

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: statistics share an axis anywhere in this figure. The claim does not rest on this figure alone: F2 reaches the same conclusion from 8 within-arm degrees of freedom without using

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: the floor at all. Panels (b) and (c) sit side by side because the channel is quoted as a paired within-run difference and rank is not - there is no paired form of "this run has

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a
